problem_type: Project library sync badge reports missing assets and then refuses to open the project
symptom: v0.22.0 user feedback: the project card shows a missing-assets badge and clicking the card (continue creating) only opens the sync popover; the project can never be entered because re-checking cannot bring the files back.
direct_cause: ProjectLibraryPage.openProject returned early for every status other than ready, and inspectWorkspaceSync resolved every nomi-local reference in the manifest against this folder, including assets that belong to another project (dragged in from All assets), so a borrowed asset was counted as missing forever.
class_root: The library pre-check became a second owner of whether a project can open, and its asset count ignored the project id that every nomi-local URL carries as its ownership authority.
affected_population: Users who dragged assets from another project into the current project through the All assets library
Users whose project folder genuinely lost one or more asset files
Users opening a project whose manifest needs backup recovery through the normal open flow
entry_points: nomi:workspace:sync-inspect IPC for the library badge and the manual re-check
internal_only_reason: Both the asset ownership rule (URL project id) and the open gate are application-owned; no third-party behavior decides them.

invariant_owner_layer.why: projectSyncFace already owns the status table (badge wording and tone); whether a status stops continue-creating now lives next to it as syncStatusBlocksOpen, and inspectWorkspaceSync owns which references belong to this folder.

invariants: Only references whose URL project id equals the inspected project are counted as this folder's assets.
Missing assets and unreadable manifests never block opening; the open flow and per-node media states own those.
Only external-change stops continue-creating, and its popover re-check adopts the new revision and releases the gate.

door_reduction.why_not: The read doors only pass the inspection shape through; the write doors are distinct: the IPC is the only caller that inspects a folder, referencedAssetPaths is the only collector of owned references, and the library card is the only place that decides whether to stop before opening. Each now reads one owner.

generality_proof: The project id comes from the registry id the IPC already resolves, which is the same id the nomi-local protocol uses to find files, so every entry that creates a cross-project reference (drag from All assets, Agent import, paste) is covered without listing them.

shared_boundaries.responsibility: Collect only this project's nomi-local references, decoded per segment like the protocol.
Decide which sync statuses stop continue-creating.

same_class_entry_points.evidence: openProject consults syncStatusBlocksOpen instead of status !== ready.
The re-check still calls the same IPC, which now counts only owned references.

recurrence.reason: Any new way of referencing another project's asset, or any real file loss, would again lock the project behind a gate with no exit.

prevention.invariant: The library never becomes a second owner of project openability.
prevention.failure_mode: Unit tests fail if a borrowed asset is counted as missing; the real library walk (probe recorded in the PR) opens a project with a genuinely missing file.
prevention.strategy: Derive asset ownership from the URL project id and keep the open-gate rule in the status table.

legacy_paths.rationale: openProject's blanket status !== 'ready' gate is replaced by syncStatusBlocksOpen in the same change.

migration: No persisted state changes; the sync baseline format is unchanged.
residual_risks: A project whose borrowed asset's source project was deleted still shows that card as failed to load inside the canvas; that is honest per-node state, not a library gate.
